newsitem.title: USA: AMEX to bid for NYSE options business shortly.
newsitem.headline: AMEX to bid for NYSE options business shortly.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange will "very shortly" submit a proposal to the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) to buy NYSE's equity options business, AMEX executive vice president of derivatives Joseph Stefanelli said.
"We're certainly very interested in being the winner in this sweepstakes," Stefanelli told Reuters in an interview.
"Our initial goal is to try to offer NYSE a proposal that will put the current membership in the most favorable position than any other proposal."

He said the offer would be made "very shortly", but declined to disclose when. He was also unable to disclose the financial term for the possible purchase. Earlier this year, NYSE said it was considering selling off its equity options business.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), which has the lion's share of the U.S. equity options business, as well as the New York Cotton Exchange have already shown interest in NYSE's business.
Stefanelli said the physical proximity of NYSE and AMEX should be an advantage.

"The most important factor is to disrupt the lives of the current membership as little as possible," he said. "In purchasing the business, we're not just focusing on the options. We're looking at bringing their membership to trade on our floor."
He said AMEX's offer was "very realistic and very competitive".
"We want them over here to be productive and to be here for an extended period of time and feel comfortable in assimilating into our membership," Stefanelli noted.
